case_name: C. Sankaranarayanan Etc. v State Of Kerala
respondent:
State Of Kerala
Supreme Court of India

4  May  1971
CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION: C.As. Nos. 1789 to 1791 of 1969. Appeals by special leave from the judgments and orders Dt. 11 June 1969, and 10 July 1969 of the Kerala High Court in Writ Appeals Nos. 126 of 1968 and 762 of 1969.
The Judgment was delivered by : A. N. Grover, J.
1. These appeals by special leave are from a judgment of a division bench of the Kerala High Court.-affirming the decision of a learned single judge who had dismissed the writ petitions of the appellants.
The appellant in C.A. 1789/69 entered service as a teacher in a private aided school on March 14, 1946. Both the appellants in C.A. 1790/69 had joined service originally as teachers in aided schools but they entered government school service on August 17, 1958 and December 13, 1948 respectively. Similarly in C.A. 1791/69 the appellant joined government service as a teacher and attained the age of 55 on July 2, 1968.
2. It appears that
facts: The appellant in C.A. 1789/69 entered service as a teacher in a private aided school on March 14, 1946.
Both the appellants in C.A. 1790/69 had joined service originally as teachers in aided schools but they entered government school service on August 17, 1958 and December 13, 1948 respectively.
Similarly in C.A. 1791/69 the appellant joined government service as a teacher and attained the age of 55 on July 2, 1968.
On November 22, 1965 all associations of government and private aided school teachers of which the appellants were members submitted a memorandum to the government making various demands.
One of these (No. 11) was that the age of retirement of school teachers should be raised to 60 years.
On July 14, 1966 the government issued an order by which the age of retirement was raised from 55 to 58 years.

The necessary amendments were formally made both in the Kerala Education Rules framed under the Act 6 of 1959 and the Kerala Service Rules made by the Governor in exercise of the powers conferred by the proviso to Art. 309 of the Constitution.
issues: Mutual exclusivity of Chapters XXVII-A and B
Applicability of Rule 8 in Chapter XXVII-A
Government's power to make rules regulating conditions of service
Estoppel or binding agreement between government and teachers
petitioner_arguments: The provisions of Chapters XXVII-A and B were not mutually exclusive.
He was entitled to the benefit of Rule 8 in Chapter XXVII-A.
As he was in service of an aided school prior to September 4, 1957 his age of retirement of superannuation was to be 60 years.
respondent_arguments: The provisions of Chapters XXVII-A and B were mutually exclusive.
He was not entitled to the benefit of Rule 8 in Chapter XXVII-A.
As he was a teacher in an aided school, the age of compulsory retirement by virtue of Rule 4 of Chapter XXVIIB would be the same as that of teachers of government schools.
court_reasoning: The approach of the division bench was that the provisions of Chapters XXVII-A and B when read together leave no doubt that the two chapters are mutually exclusive.
Chapter XXVIIB makes independent and separate provisions which are inconsistent with those contained in Chapter XXVIIA.
As the appellant in C.A. 1789/69 is a teacher in an aided school, the age of compulsory retirement by virtue of Rule 4 of Chapter XXVIIB would be the same as that of teachers of government schools.
The rule of estoppel can hardly be invoked in the circumstances of the case.

In Union of India & Ors. v. M/s. Indo-Afghan Agencies Ltd., [1968] 2 S.C.R. 366, this Court held that where a person had acted upon the representation made in the export promotion scheme that import licence upto the value of the goods exported would be issued and had actually exported goods his claim for an import licence for the maximum value permissible by the scheme could not be arbitrarily rejected.

Even though s. 115 of the Evidence Act was not in terms applicable it was still open to the respondent who had acted on that representation to claim that the government should be bound to carry out the promise made by it though not recorded in the form of a formal contract as required by the Constitution.
holding: The age of compulsory retirement for the appellant would be 55 years, same as that of teachers of government schools.
The principle of estoppel or binding agreement between government and teachers cannot be invoked.
